questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of discontinuous variation?
options: The feature can take any numerical value within a continuous range.
The feature falls into distinct, limited categories with no intermediates.
The feature is displayed using a line graph instead of a bar chart.
The feature is only ever influenced by the surrounding environment.

questions.question: How is continuous variation best described?
options: Features that can be grouped into a small number of distinct categories.
Features that are either completely present or completely absent.
Features that can take any value within a wide, unbroken range.
Features that are determined solely by a single gene and do not change.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies a continuous feature followed by a discontinuous feature in humans?
options: Height and blood group
Blood group and eye colour
Lobed ears and height
Eye colour and weight

questions.question: Which type of chart is most appropriate for displaying continuous data, such as the body mass of a population of mice?
options: A pie chart
A bar chart with gaps between bars
A histogram
A Venn diagram

questions.question: Which of the following best explains what influences a continuous variation feature like a person's height?
options: It is determined entirely by a single gene inherited from the mother.
It is influenced by a combination of genetics, nutrition, and general lifestyle.
It is affected only by the physical environment after birth.
It is determined solely by the lifestyle choices made during adulthood.

questions.question: When displaying data for a discontinuous feature, such as blood groups in a classroom, which type of chart should be used?
options: A line graph with a line of best fit
A scatter graph
A histogram with touching bars
A bar chart with gaps between the bars

questions.question: What is typically true about the cause of discontinuous variation?
options: It is usually caused only by genetic factors and is unaffected by lifestyle.
It is heavily influenced by diet, exercise, and climate.
It changes constantly throughout an organism's lifetime.
It is caused entirely by environmental conditions during development.

questions.question: When a pair of domestic cats reproduce, they always produce kittens rather than puppies or rabbit kits. What is this concept known as?
options: Discontinuous variation
Species resemblance
Environmental adaptation
Continuous distribution

questions.question: Why do siblings in a human family often look similar to each other and to their parents?
options: Because they inherit genetic features from both parents, leading to family resemblance.
Because they share the exact same environmental influences throughout their entire lives.
Because siblings are genetically identical to their father.
Because children only inherit physical features from their mother.

questions.question: What molecule is passed from parents to offspring during reproduction to transmit inherited features?
options: Glucose
DNA
Haemoglobin
Hormones

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding variation among offspring from the same parents?
options: Offspring are always exact clones of one of their parents.
Offspring from the same parents are completely identical to one another.
There is usually variation, meaning offspring are not typically identical to their parents or siblings.
Offspring never share any features with their parents.

questions.question: How do differences between individuals of different species compare to differences between individuals of the same species?
options: Differences within a species are always much greater than differences between species.
There are absolutely no differences between individuals of different species.
Differences between species are greater than differences within species.
The level of difference is exactly the same in both cases.

questions.question: What is the biological term used to describe the differences in features between individuals belonging to the same species?
options: Variation
Classification
Resemblance
Adaptation

questions.question: Which of the following features is an example of variation caused solely by the environment?
options: Having natural blue eyes
Having an O-positive blood group
Having a scar from a childhood injury
Having curly hair

questions.question: Which variation in humans is determined solely by inherited genetic information in the genome?
options: Having a suntan
Your blood group
Body weight
Speaking a particular language

questions.question: Which of the following features is determined by a combination of both genetic inheritance and environmental or lifestyle factors?
options: ABO blood group
Biological sex
Body mass
Presence of earlobes
